name: AI Governance Review — Demonstration
oneLiner: [DEMO] A worked example of how I would review an AI product before launch: data use, terms, oversight, and risk.
question: What would a rigorous but proportionate pre-launch review look like for a small AI product — and can a student produce one worth reading?
problem: [DEMO] Small teams ship AI features without any structured look at data use, terms, oversight, or risk — not from malice, but because review frameworks are written for enterprises and read like compliance theater. The demonstration subject is 'VoiceNote KH', a fictional app that transcribes Khmer voice messages using a fine-tuned speech model.
targetUsers: [DEMO] The review's audience: a small product team deciding whether the fictional VoiceNote KH is ready for a public beta — and what must change first.
whyItMatters: This demonstration exists because pillar four needs to be shown, not asserted. The format — scope, evidence, findings, required changes, and an artifact — is the real content; the app under review is fictional and labeled as such throughout.
exactRole: Author of the demonstration review, applying frameworks I am studying (model cards, data-protection basics, terms-of-service analysis) to a fictional product.
teamContributions: None — this is an individual demonstration exercise, not a client engagement or a real audit.
research: [DEMO] The review method draws on public model-card practice, data-minimization principles, and how consumer transcription products describe retention and consent in their terms. Sources are the kind a real review would cite; the findings apply them to a fictional app.
validation: This is a demonstration: it validates the review format, not any real product. Nothing here has been applied to a real company, and no real product decisions rest on it.
proposedSolution: [DEMO] A four-part review: (1) what data the product touches and why; (2) what its terms promise versus what the system does; (3) where humans approve consequential outcomes; (4) a risk register with proportionate mitigations. The deliverable is a model card the team must be able to publish honestly.
userWorkflow: Scope the review: features, data flows, users, and jurisdictions
Trace every personal-data touchpoint against the stated purpose
Compare the drafted terms and privacy notice with actual system behavior
Map decision points to human approvals and audit records
Deliver findings as required changes, recommendations, and an honest model card
systemArchitecture: [DEMO] The review treats architecture as evidence: where audio is processed, where transcripts are stored, what leaves the device, and which third parties see anything. For VoiceNote KH the finding is typical of small products — the architecture is fine; the retention defaults and consent copy are not.
methods: Structured review practice: claim → argument → evidence for every finding, severity ratings tied to user harm rather than legal exposure alone, and the discipline that a finding without a required change is just commentary.
businessValue: [DEMO] For a real product, this review would be launch insurance: cheaper than retrofitting consent flows after a complaint, and a trust asset when users ask hard questions. As a demonstration, its value is showing I can produce the artifact.
contractsPolicy: [DEMO] Sample findings of the demonstration: the draft terms claimed a perpetual license to voice recordings the product does not need (required change: license scoped to service delivery); the consent copy bundled transcription with model-improvement use (required change: separate opt-in).
dataPrivacy: [DEMO] Sample findings: default retention was indefinite where the feature needs days (required change: retention schedule with user deletion); voice data crossed a border without disclosure (required change: state processing locations in plain language).
risks: [DEMO] For the fictional product: silent misuse of voice data for model training; indefinite retention; no path for users to delete recordings; over-broad license terms
For the demonstration itself: being mistaken for legal advice or a real audit — it is neither, and says so
humanApprovalPoints: [DEMO] In the reviewed product: shipping any change to data use or terms; enabling model-improvement use of customer audio; responding to data-deletion requests
In a real engagement: every finding would be reviewed by someone with actual legal authority before any action
technicalDecisions: Review format anchored on a publishable model card, so honesty has a concrete deliverable
Findings must pair with required changes and proportionate mitigations
Severity rated by user harm, not only compliance exposure
The demonstration subject is fictional so no real company's practices are implied

completedWork.text: Complete demonstration review of the fictional VoiceNote KH, including the model-card artifact on this page
The same format applied to a real CHNAI LAB product before its release

evidence.text: Everything in this case study is a demonstration built on a fictional product. It shows the review format I am practicing — it is not a real audit, and no real product or company is described.
The governance patterns referenced here (human-approval gates, audit design) run in real code in Chomkar Decision Grid.

results.text: The demonstration produced a complete review with findings, required changes, and a publishable model card — the artifact below is the deliverable itself, not a description of one.

constraints: The reviewed product is fictional, so findings cannot be validated against real system behavior
I am a student of these frameworks — a real engagement would need supervision by someone with actual legal and privacy expertise
tradeoffs: A fictional subject removes confidentiality problems but also removes the messy details that make real reviews hard
Keeping the review proportionate for a small team means it is not an exhaustive compliance audit — by design

lessonsLearned: A model card forces more honesty than a policy document — you cannot write 'purpose' and 'retention' rows vaguely and still publish them
Terms-versus-behavior comparison finds more real issues than reading either alone
Review findings only matter if each one carries a required change someone can act on
nextValidation: Apply the same review format to a real CHNAI LAB product before its release
Have the resulting review checked by a supervising practitioner with real legal expertise
Publish the before/after: what the review changed in the shipped product

artifact.title: Model card — VoiceNote KH (fictional demonstration subject)
artifact.description: The review's deliverable: a model card the fictional team could publish honestly after making the required changes. Every row is demonstration content.

rows.label: Purpose
rows.value: Transcribe Khmer voice messages to text for the message recipient. No other use of audio without separate opt-in.

rows.label: Users
rows.value: Khmer-speaking adults messaging within the app; not offered to children.

rows.label: Model
rows.value: Fine-tuned Whisper-family speech model; quality self-reported by internal evaluation, not independently benchmarked.

rows.label: Data sources
rows.value: User voice messages processed at request time; training data licensed separately and documented in the data register.

rows.label: Retention
rows.value: Audio deleted after transcription completes; transcripts kept until the user deletes the message. No indefinite retention.

rows.label: Consent
rows.value: Transcription is core service consent; model-improvement use requires a separate, revocable opt-in.

rows.label: Human oversight
rows.value: No automated account actions from transcript content; abuse reports are reviewed by a person.

rows.label: Known limitations
rows.value: Accuracy degrades with noise, code-switching, and underrepresented dialects; users can always fall back to audio.

rows.label: Risk level & escalation
rows.value: Moderate (personal voice data). Data-deletion requests and suspected breaches escalate to a named accountable owner.

aiAssistance.scope: Claude assisted with drafting the review structure and this case study's prose.
